answer: Make trust expensive to grow and cheap to lose: an agent starts with a tiny transaction limit, and only signed, completed work from independent counterparties raises that limit, one verified job at a time, like a reef growing coral by coral. Forging a thousand fake identities therefore means paying for a thousand real work histories, not just minting names. A single fraud then causes a ripple of slashing across the linked stake of that identity, so an attacker loses a saffron-priced reputation faster than it can be rebuilt.
